content.text:
Git: Read, search and manipulate local Git repositories from your AI assistant.
By MCP reference servers. Developer Tools. Verified by mcp.tc: official server from MCP reference servers.
Listing page: https://mcp.tc/i/git
Install command: uvx mcp-server-git --repository /path/to/repo
Access: Runs on your computer, started by your client.
Connects an assistant to a local Git repository so it can read history and state, search content, and make changes through Git operations. It is one of the reference servers maintained in the modelcontextprotocol/servers repository. Runs locally over stdio, started with uvx (uvx mcp-server-git --repository /path/to/repo), with pip (python -m mcp_server_git) or with Docker (mcp/git image, with the repository mounted). No sign-in or API key is required. It works on repositories on your own…
History (new PyPI versions checked every 3 hours, tools not read): no change recorded yet. https://mcp.tc/i/git#history
Setup (call get_server with client=<id> for the full steps):
- Claude Code (claude-code): `claude mcp add --transport stdio git -- uvx mcp-server-git --repository /path/to/repo`
- Claude Desktop (claude-desktop): see client=claude-desktop
- Cursor (cursor): Add to Cursor: https://cursor.com/install-mcp?name=git&config=eyJjb21tYW5kIjoidXZ4IiwiYXJncyI6WyJtY3Atc2VydmVyLWdpdCIsIi0tcmVwb3NpdG9yeSIsIi9wYXRoL3RvL3JlcG8iXX0%3D
- VS Code (vscode): `code --add-mcp '{"name":"git","type":"stdio","command":"uvx","args":["mcp-server-git","--repository","/path/to/repo"]}'`
- Devin Desktop (devin): see client=devin
- Codex (codex): `codex mcp add git -- uvx mcp-server-git --repository /path/to/repo`
- Gemini CLI (gemini): `gemini mcp add git uvx -- mcp-server-git --repository /path/to/repo`
- Any client (json): see client=json

setup.label: Claude Code
setup.quick: `claude mcp add --transport stdio git -- uvx mcp-server-git --repository /path/to/repo`
steps: Run this in a terminal, in your project folder:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport stdio git -- uvx mcp-server-git --repository /path/to/repo
```
Start Claude Code and type `/mcp`. **git** should show as connected.
setup.code: claude mcp add --transport stdio git -- uvx mcp-server-git --repository /path/to/repo
setup.note: Add `--scope user` to make it available in every project.

setup.label: Claude Desktop
steps: Open **Settings → Developer → Edit Config**. It opens `claude_desktop_config.json`. Add:
Save the file and restart Claude Desktop.
setup.note: Needs uv (Python) on your computer. The file lives in `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/` on macOS and `%APPDATA%\Claude\` on Windows.

setup.label: Cursor
steps: Add to Cursor: https://cursor.com/install-mcp?name=git&config=eyJjb21tYW5kIjoidXZ4IiwiYXJncyI6WyJtY3Atc2VydmVyLWdpdCIsIi0tcmVwb3NpdG9yeSIsIi9wYXRoL3RvL3JlcG8iXX0%3D
Or add it by hand to `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (all projects) or `.cursor/mcp.json` (this project):

setup.label: VS Code
steps: Install in VS Code: https://vscode.dev/redirect/mcp/install?name=git&config=%7B%22type%22%3A%22stdio%22%2C%22command%22%3A%22uvx%22%2C%22args%22%3A%5B%22mcp-server-git%22%2C%22--repository%22%2C%22%2Fpath%2Fto%2Frepo%22%5D%7D
Or from a terminal:

```bash
code --add-mcp '{"name":"git","type":"stdio","command":"uvx","args":["mcp-server-git","--repository","/path/to/repo"]}'
```
Or commit it to the repo in `.vscode/mcp.json`:

setup.label: Devin Desktop
steps: Add it to `~/.config/devin/mcp_config.json` (macOS and Linux) or `%APPDATA%\devin\mcp_config.json` (Windows):
Refresh the MCP server list in Cascade.
setup.note: Devin Desktop is the new name for Windsurf.

setup.label: Codex
steps:
```bash
codex mcp add git -- uvx mcp-server-git --repository /path/to/repo
```
Or edit `~/.codex/config.toml` directly:

```toml
[mcp_servers.git]
command = "uvx"
args = ["mcp-server-git", "--repository", "/path/to/repo"]
```
setup.code: codex mcp add git -- uvx mcp-server-git --repository /path/to/repo

setup.label: Gemini CLI
steps:
```bash
gemini mcp add git uvx -- mcp-server-git --repository /path/to/repo
```
setup.code: gemini mcp add git uvx -- mcp-server-git --repository /path/to/repo
setup.note: This adds it to the current project. Add `-s user` to use it everywhere.
